name: OKC_ARTICLE_VERSIONS
description: This table stores all the versions of a standard clause and non-standard clause created on a business document. Standard Clauses have multiple versions while the non-standard clauses are created as a single version. This table replaces the OKC_STD_ART_VERSIONS available in releases prior to 11.5.10. Furthermore, the non- standard clause text in OKC_K_ARTICLES_TL is migrated to this table as a part of 11.5.10 migration.

columns.name: ARTICLE_VERSION_ID
columns.description: System generated Primary Key.

columns.name: OBJECT_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.description: Used to implement optimistic locking. This number is incremented every time that the row is updated. The number is compared at the start and end of a transaction to detect whether another session has updated the row since it was queried.

columns.name: ARTICLE_ID
columns.description: This references the Clause for which this version is created. Foreign Key to OKC_ARTICLES_ALL.

columns.name: ARTICLE_VERSION_NUMBER
columns.description: This is the system generated version number of the clause. Sequence begins at 1.

columns.name: ARTICLE_TEXT
columns.description: This is the textual content of the clause including the embedded variables.

columns.name: PROVISION_YN
columns.description: Yes/No flag  to indicate whether the clause is provision or not i.e. if  Y then Provision, if N then Clause.

columns.name: INSERT_BY_REFERENCE
columns.description: Yes/No flag  to determine the text that will be printed i.e. if  Y then clause should be printed without the clause text, if N then the clause text is printed.

columns.name: LOCK_TEXT
columns.description: Yes/No flag  to indicate whether the clause text can be modified on a business document ( this flag determines whether user can modify a standard clause to create a non-standard clause).

columns.name: GLOBAL_YN
columns.description: Yes/No flag  to indicate whether the clause is global or not i.e. if  Y then Global , if N then Local.

columns.name: ARTICLE_LANGUAGE
columns.description: This is the language of the Clause. Same as that of OKC_ARTICLES_ALL as it is required for text index.

columns.name: ARTICLE_STATUS
columns.description: This is the status of standard clause. This is a foreign key to FND_LOOKUPS with LOOKUP_TYPE = OKC_ARTICLE_STATUS.

columns.name: SAV_RELEASE
columns.description: This is the user entered release label prior to 11.5.10.  Kept for backward compatibility for migrated clauses.

columns.name: START_DATE
columns.description: This is the Effective Start Date of the  Standard Clause Version.

columns.name: END_DATE
columns.description: This is the Effective End Date of the  Standard Clause Version.

columns.name: ADOPTION_TYPE
columns.description: This is the adoption type of the local clause. It could either be LOCALIZED (same as the adoption type of OKC_ARTICLE_ADOPTIONS) or LOCAL.

columns.name: STD_ARTICLE_VERSION_ID
columns.description: This references the standard clause  version that was modified to create a non-standard clause. This is a foreign key to OKC_ARTICLE_VERSIONS.

columns.name: DISPLAY_NAME
columns.description: This is the clause name that will be printed or displayed in a business document. If this column is not populated , the clause title will be used.

columns.name: TRANSLATED_YN
columns.description: Yes/No flag  to indicate whether the clause is created as a translation of global clause or not.

columns.name: ARTICLE_DESCRIPTION
columns.description: This is a short description of the Clause Version.

columns.name: DATE_APPROVED
columns.description: This is the approval date of the clause.

columns.name: DEFAULT_SECTION
columns.description: This is the default section to which the clause belongs. Foreign Key to FND_LOOKUPS where Lookup_Type = OKC_ARTICLE_SECTION.

columns.name: REFERENCE_SOURCE
columns.description: This is the reference source of the clause if the Insert By Reference column is Yes e.g. website/publication etc.

columns.name: REFERENCE_TEXT
columns.description: This is the reference text of the clause if the Insert By Reference column is Yes e.g. website/publication etc.

columns.name: ORIG_SYSTEM_REFERENCE_CODE
columns.description: This column is used to preserve the code for the migrated system.

columns.name: ORIG_SYSTEM_REFERENCE_ID1
columns.description: This column is used to preserve the identifier1 for the migrated system.

columns.name: ORIG_SYSTEM_REFERENCE_ID2
columns.description: This column is used to preserve the identifier2 for the migrated system.

columns.name: ADDITIONAL_INSTRUCTIONS
columns.description: This column stores any additional instructions that are needed  for using the Clause Version.

columns.name: VARIATION_DESCRIPTION
columns.description: This is used in the case of non-standard clauses to enter variations from Standard Clauses prior to 11.5.10. This column is kept for backward compatibility.

columns.name: CREATED_BY
columns.description: Who column: indicates the user who created the row.

columns.name: CREATION_DATE
columns.description: Who column: indicates the date and time of the creation of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_DATE
columns.description: Who column: indicates the date and time of the last update of the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATED_BY
columns.description: Who column: indicates the user who last updated the row.

columns.name: LAST_UPDATE_LOGIN
columns.description: Who column: indicates the session login associated to the user who last updated the row.

columns.name: PROGRAM_NAME
columns.description: Identifies the concurrent program

columns.name: PROGRAM_APP_NAME
columns.description: Identifies the Application name spawning the Concurrent Request
